Dodanim
dō'da-nim
n. pl. (the fourth-named people descended from Javan, a maritime branch of the sons of Japheth)
From Hebrew Dodanim, a plural gentilic — the name of a people, not of a single man. Some Hebrew copies read Rodanim, the letters daleth and resh being nearly identical in the older script; the KJV follows Dodanim in both places.

Biblical Definition

Dodanim closes the short list of Javan's descendants: “And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim” (Gen 10:4), and the Chronicler copies it exactly (1Ch 1:7). The form is plural, as with Kittim beside it, which tells the reader that the table of nations is not tracking individuals only but the clans that came from them — the genealogy has already begun to shade into geography. All four names in Javan's column belong to the sea. They are the peoples of whom the very next verse says: “By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations” (Gen 10:5). Nothing else is said of the Dodanim anywhere in Scripture. They are a coastland people among the far islands, holding, in the Bible's own reckoning, the outer edge of the known world. That edge matters. When Isaiah speaks of the isles that have not heard the LORD's fame and shall yet declare His glory, and when the prophets speak of the isles waiting for His law, these are the peoples in view — the ones furthest from Zion, named in Genesis before anyone had thought of going to them.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Dodanim; in sacred geography they are a people descended from Javan and settled among the isles of the Gentiles.

expand to see more

DODANIM, n. plu. A people descended from Javan, the son of Japheth.

They are named with Elishah, Tarshish and Kittim, all maritime nations.

The name is a plural form, denoting a family or clan rather than a single ancestor.

Some copies read Rodanim, the letters being of like form in the ancient character.

They are reckoned among the isles of the Gentiles, divided after their tongues and nations.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:4 — "And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim."

1Ch 1:7 — "And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim."

Gen 10:5 — "By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations."

Gen 10:32 — "These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations: and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood."

Modern Corruption

A variant spelling in the Hebrew copies is offered as evidence that the text is corrupt and its history unreliable; the variation is real, trivial, and exactly the kind of thing faithful preservation looks like.

expand to see more

Dodanim is a favourite small exhibit in the case against the reliability of the Old Testament text, because some Hebrew and versional copies read Rodanim. The two Hebrew letters involved differ by the length of a stroke. The dictionary's doctrine of preservation has never claimed that no copyist ever mistook daleth for resh; it claims that God has kept His word pure in all ages so that nothing necessary to faith or life has been lost. A variant that changes one consonant in the name of an unmentioned coastal people is not a wound to that doctrine. It is a demonstration of how narrow the real margin is: the copies that differ on Dodanim agree on the ten commandments, the Servant of Isaiah 53, and every promise the church lives by.

The second corruption is subtler and belongs to the reader rather than the critic — treating the far coastlands as background scenery. The whole force of Genesis 10 is that it lists nations Israel would never meet, whose names no Israelite could locate, and that the God of Abraham is already their God by right of creation and judgment. The isles are not the end of the map; they are part of the inheritance promised to the Son: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession” (Psa 2:8). Missions did not begin at Antioch. It began as a claim staked in a genealogy.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Dodanim (H1721), Dodanim; 'iy (H339), isle, coastland; Yavan (H3120), Javan; lashon (H3956), tongue, language; goy (H1471), nation.

expand to see more

Hebrew Dodanim (H1721) — Dodanim; a plural gentilic naming a people descended from Javan.

Hebrew Yavan (H3120) — Javan; their father, the head of the Greek and Aegean peoples.

Hebrew 'iy (H339) — isle, coastland; the “isles of the Gentiles” of Gen 10:5.

Hebrew lashon (H3956) — tongue, language; the mark by which the families were divided.

Hebrew mishpachah (H4940) — family, clan; the plural form of the name points to this unit.

Usage

"“Kittim, and Dodanim” — two plural names in a list of men, where genealogy turns into geography."

"“The isles of the Gentiles” — the far edge of the world, named before anyone sailed to it."

"A single-consonant variant, and every doctrine untouched."
